claims.text: Tungsten carbide-based cermet can be used to fabricate sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates for hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Tungsten carbide-based cermet decreases localized corrosion caused by molten aluminum.
Using tungsten carbide-based cermet extends the service life of hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Conventional metal components, including steel rollers, are susceptible to corrosion by molten aluminum during hot-dip plating.
Tungsten carbide has sufficient chemical inertia to limit dissolution or chemical attack by aluminum at elevated temperatures.
Tungsten carbide has high inherent hardness.
The chemical affinity between tungsten carbide-based cermet and molten aluminum is lower than that between conventional steel and molten aluminum.
Reduced chemical affinity between tungsten carbide-based cermet and molten aluminum lowers the corrosion rate.
The hardness of tungsten carbide-based cermet increases component wear resistance.
Minimizing corrosion and mechanical wear from molten-aluminum contact produces longer component service life.
Conventional steel exhibits significant corrosion in molten-aluminum environments.
Conventional steel wears quickly in molten-aluminum environments.
Rapid corrosion and wear of conventional steel lead to frequent component replacement.
Prolonged exposure, higher temperatures, or more aggressive chemical environments may require additional protection or specialized cermet formulations.
The magnitude of service-life improvement and the cost-effectiveness of tungsten carbide-based cermet remain undetermined without testing across process parameters and alloy compositions.
